name: Speech Recognition
definition: The ability to identify and understand the speech of another person.

benchmark.name: LibriSpeech
benchmark.model_or_system: Conformer XXL+ with noisy student training and wav2vec 2.0 pre-training (Zhang et al., Google)
benchmark.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult listeners and working transcribers: fluent English speakers doing careful verbatim transcription of recorded speech

benchmark.name: LibriSpeech
benchmark.model_or_system: Conformer XXL with wav2vec 2.0 pre-training and noisy student training (Google Brain, Zhang et al.)
benchmark.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-clean, lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult listeners, with typical non-professional human transcribers as the practical comparison. Speech recognition is a general ability used across most jobs.

benchmark.name: LibriSpeech
benchmark.model_or_system: Conformer XXL+ with wav2vec 2.0 pre-training and noisy student training (Zhang et al., Google)
benchmark.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult working population: typical fluent listeners who identify and understand the speech of others at work. Proxied by non-expert human transcribers.

benchmark.name: LibriSpeech
benchmark.model_or_system: Conformer XXL, wav2vec 2.0 pre-trained + noisy student training with SpecAugment (Zhang et al., Google)
benchmark.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other (lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: English-proficient adults doing careful word-level transcription of read speech (general educated workforce and non-specialist transcribers)

benchmark.name: Open ASR Leaderboard
benchmark.metric: average word error rate (%) across the leaderboard's English short-form test sets; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce of fluent English listeners who must identify and understand others' speech at work. Non-specialist human transcription accuracy is used as the proxy.

benchmark.name: Open ASR Leaderboard
benchmark.metric: average word error rate (%) across the English short-form datasets; lower is better
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: people who must accurately identify spoken words in work settings, such as meetings, calls, lectures and dictation. Careful non-specialist listeners are the median, with professional transcribers as the upper end.

benchmark.name: Open ASR Leaderboard
benchmark.model_or_system: ARK-ASR-3B (listed as Edge0/ARK-ASR-3B, a copy of AutoArk-AI/ARK-ASR-3B)
benchmark.metric: mean word error rate, % (lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical fluent English listeners who must identify spoken words in everyday work settings such as meetings, calls and speeches. Professional transcribers are used as an upper-end check.
